**TEST FOR COMBINATIONS OF DATA**
```{r}
library(GEOquery)
library(limma)
library(dplyr)
library(sva)
library(tidyr)

# 1. Define your Master List
gse_ids <- c("GSE32628", "GSE45164", "GSE45216", "GSE98767")
target_genes <- c("TWIST1", "OVOL1")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 1: PRE-DOWNLOAD & PRE-PROCESS INDIVIDUALS
# ----------------------------------------------------------------
# Store processed data in a list to avoid re-downloading in loops
processed_data <- lapply(gse_ids, function(id) {
  message("Pre-processing: ", id)
  gse <- getGEO(id, destdir = ".", getGPL = TRUE)[[1]]
  exprs_mat <- exprs(gse)
  meta <- pData(gse)
  
  if (max(exprs_mat, na.rm=T) > 50) exprs_mat <- log2(exprs_mat + 1)
  
  # Standardize Metadata
  meta <- meta %>%
    mutate(Condition = case_when(
      grepl("normal|control", paste(title, source_name_ch1), ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "NS",
      grepl("keratosis|AK", paste(title, source_name_ch1), ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "AK",
      grepl("carcinoma|SCC", paste(title, source_name_ch1), ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "cSCC",
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    )) %>%
    filter(Condition != "Other") %>%
    mutate(Batch = id, SampleID = rownames(.))
  
  # Map Genes
  fdata <- fData(gse)
  sym_col <- grep("SYMBOL|Gene.Symbol", colnames(fdata), ignore.case = TRUE, value = TRUE)[1]
  mapping <- fdata %>% select(ID, Symbol = !!sym_col) %>% 
    mutate(Symbol = gsub(" ///.*", "", Symbol)) %>% filter(Symbol %in% target_genes)
  
  sub_ex <- exprs_mat[as.character(mapping$ID), colnames(exprs_mat) %in% rownames(meta), drop=FALSE]
  rownames(sub_ex) <- mapping$Symbol
  return(list(exprs = avereps(sub_ex), meta = meta))
})
names(processed_data) <- gse_ids

# ----------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 2: ROBUST COMBINATORIAL LOOP
# ----------------------------------------------------------------
results_list <- list()

for (i in 1:length(gse_ids)) {
  combos <- combn(gse_ids, i, simplify = FALSE)
  
  for (subset_ids in combos) {
    combo_name <- paste(subset_ids, collapse = " + ")
    message("Testing Combination: ", combo_name)
    
    current_list <- processed_data[subset_ids]
    common_genes <- Reduce(intersect, lapply(current_list, function(x) rownames(x$exprs)))
    
    if(!all(c("TWIST1", "OVOL1") %in% common_genes)) next
    
    merged_exprs <- do.call(cbind, lapply(current_list, function(x) x$exprs[common_genes, ]))
    merged_meta <- do.call(rbind, lapply(current_list, function(x) x$meta %>% select(Condition, Batch)))
    
    # --- BATCH CORRECTION WITH SINGULARITY CHECK ---
    final_exprs <- merged_exprs
    if (length(subset_ids) > 1) {
      merged_meta$Condition <- as.factor(merged_meta$Condition)
      merged_meta$Batch <- as.factor(merged_meta$Batch)
      
      # Check if 'Condition' has more than 1 level and isn't confounded with 'Batch'
      # If a condition only exists in one batch, we can't use it in the model
      condition_counts <- table(merged_meta$Condition, merged_meta$Batch)
      is_singular <- any(rowSums(condition_counts > 0) < 2) 
      
      tryCatch({
        if (is_singular) {
          message("  ! Confounding detected. Running ComBat without Condition adjustment.")
          # Use an intercept-only model if groups don't overlap across batches
          mod_null <- model.matrix(~1, data = merged_meta)
          final_exprs <- ComBat(dat = merged_exprs, batch = merged_meta$Batch, mod = mod_null)
        } else {
          mod <- model.matrix(~Condition, data = merged_meta)
          final_exprs <- ComBat(dat = merged_exprs, batch = merged_meta$Batch, mod = mod)
        }
      }, error = function(e) {
        message("  ! ComBat failed for ", combo_name, ". Using uncorrected data.")
        final_exprs <<- merged_exprs
      })
    }
    
    # --- STATISTICS ---
    cor_res <- tryCatch({
      ct <- cor.test(final_exprs["TWIST1",], final_exprs["OVOL1",], method = "pearson")
      list(r = ct$estimate, p = ct$p.value)
    }, error = function(e) list(r = NA, p = NA))
    
    results_list[[combo_name]] <- data.frame(
      Combination = combo_name,
      Num_Datasets = length(subset_ids),
      Total_Samples = ncol(final_exprs),
      Pearson_R = cor_res$r,
      P_Value = cor_res$p,
      Significant = ifelse(!is.na(cor_res$p) && cor_res$p < 0.05, "YES", "NO")
    )
  }
}

final_results_table <- do.call(rbind, results_list) %>% arrange(P_Value)
print(final_results_table)
```

```{r}
# 1. Load Libraries
library(GEOquery)
library(limma)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(sva)       # For Batch Correction (ComBat)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggpubr)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------              
# STEP 1: DEFINE DATASETS AND SETTINGS
# ----------------------------------------------------------------
gse_ids <- c("GSE32628", "GSE45164", "GSE45216")
target_genes <- c("TWIST1", "OVOL1", "KLF4", "IVL", "KRT10", "MYC")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 2: DOWNLOAD AND HARMONIZE METADATA
# ----------------------------------------------------------------
# We create a function to process each GSE so the logic is identical
process_gse <- function(id) {
  gse <- getGEO(id, destdir = ".", getGPL = TRUE)[[1]]
  exprs_mat <- exprs(gse)
  meta <- pData(gse)
  
  # Log transform if needed
  if (max(exprs_mat, na.rm=T) > 50) exprs_mat <- log2(exprs_mat + 1)
  
  # HARMONIZE CONDITION NAMES
  # This is the most important part: ensure "Normal" is same across studies
  meta <- meta %>%
    mutate(Condition = case_when(
      grepl("normal", paste(title, source_name_ch1), ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "NS",
      grepl("keratosis|AK", paste(title, source_name_ch1), ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "AK",
      grepl("carcinoma|SCC", paste(title, source_name_ch1), ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "cSCC",
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    )) %>%
    filter(Condition != "Other") %>%
    mutate(Batch = id) # Track which study the sample came from
  
  # PROBE MAPPING
  fdata <- fData(gse)
  sym_col <- grep("SYMBOL|Gene.Symbol", colnames(fdata), ignore.case = TRUE, value = TRUE)[1]
  
  mapping <- fdata %>%
    select(ID, Symbol = !!sym_col) %>%
    mutate(Symbol = gsub(" ///.*", "", Symbol)) %>%
    filter(Symbol %in% target_genes)
  
  # Subset and Average
  sub_exprs <- exprs_mat[as.character(mapping$ID), colnames(exprs_mat) %in% rownames(meta)]
  rownames(sub_exprs) <- mapping$Symbol
  clean_sub <- avereps(sub_exprs)
  
  return(list(exprs = clean_sub, meta = meta))
}

# Run the function for all IDs
data_list <- lapply(gse_ids, process_gse)
```

*CHECK FOR BATCH EFFECTS (BEFORE)*
```{r}
# MERGE RAW DATA FIRST ---
# Find common genes across all processed datasets
common_genes <- Reduce(intersect, lapply(data_list, function(x) rownames(x$exprs)))

# Combine raw expression matrices
merged_exprs <- do.call(cbind, lapply(data_list, function(x) x$exprs[common_genes, ]))

# Combine metadata
combined_meta <- do.call(rbind, lapply(data_list, function(x) {
  x$meta %>% select(Condition, Batch)
}))

# ----------------------------------------------------------------
# CHECK FOR BATCH EFFECTS (BEFORE CORRECTION)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------
# PCA on RAW merged data
pca_raw <- prcomp(t(merged_exprs), scale. = TRUE)
df_raw <- as.data.frame(pca_raw$x)
df_raw$Batch <- combined_meta$Batch
df_raw$Condition <- combined_meta$Condition

# Plotting Before
ggplot(df_raw, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = Batch, shape = Condition)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.8) +
  stat_ellipse(aes(group = Batch), linetype = 2) + 
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "PCA: Before Batch Correction", 
       subtitle = "If clusters follow 'Batch' colors, a technical bias is present")
```

```{r}
# ----------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 3: MERGE AND BATCH CORRECT
# ----------------------------------------------------------------
# Find common genes across all datasets
common_genes <- Reduce(intersect, lapply(data_list, function(x) rownames(x$exprs)))

# Combine expression matrices
combined_exprs <- do.call(cbind, lapply(data_list, function(x) x$exprs[common_genes, ]))

# Combine metadata
combined_meta <- do.call(rbind, lapply(data_list, function(x) x$meta %>% select(Condition, Batch)))

# RUN COMBAT: This removes the "Study Effect" while keeping the "Disease Effect"
mod <- model.matrix(~as.factor(Condition), data = combined_meta)
batch_corrected <- ComBat(dat = combined_exprs, batch = combined_meta$Batch, mod = mod)
```
*CHECK FOR BATCH EFFECTS*
```{r}
##VISUALIZING OUTLIERS
# Calculate PCA
pca_res <- prcomp(t(batch_corrected), scale. = TRUE)
pca_df <- as.data.frame(pca_res$x)
pca_df$Condition <- combined_meta$Condition
pca_df$Batch <- combined_meta$Batch
pca_df$SampleID <- rownames(pca_df)

# Plot PCA to spot outliers visually
ggplot(pca_df, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = Batch, shape = Condition)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.8) +
  stat_ellipse(linetype = 2) + # Ellipses help identify points outside the 95% confidence interval
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "PCA of Combined Dataset", subtitle = "Spotting multivariate outliers")

# Function to find outliers based on IQR for a specific gene
get_outliers <- function(data, gene_name) {
  vals <- data[gene_name, ]
  q1 <- quantile(vals, 0.25)
  q3 <- quantile(vals, 0.75)
  iqr <- q3 - q1
  # We use a strict 3x IQR for "extreme" outliers to avoid losing too much data
  lower_bound <- q1 - 3 * iqr
  upper_bound <- q3 + 3 * iqr
  
  outlier_samples <- names(vals[vals < lower_bound | vals > upper_bound])
  return(outlier_samples)
}

# Identify outliers for our two main genes
twist_outliers <- get_outliers(batch_corrected, "TWIST1")
ovol_outliers <- get_outliers(batch_corrected, "OVOL1")

all_outliers <- unique(c(twist_outliers, ovol_outliers))

message("Removing ", length(all_outliers), " extreme outliers: ", paste(all_outliers, collapse=", "))

# 3. Create the "Cleaned" Final Objects
final_exprs <- batch_corrected[, !colnames(batch_corrected) %in% all_outliers]
final_meta <- combined_meta[!rownames(combined_meta) %in% all_outliers, ]
```


```{r}
# ----------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 4: FINAL PLOTTING WITH NON-PARAMETRIC TESTS & FDR
# ----------------------------------------------------------------
# Use final_exprs (outlier removed) and final_meta for the cleanest stats
plot_df <- as.data.frame(t(final_exprs))
plot_df$Condition <- factor(final_meta$Condition, levels = c("NS", "AK", "cSCC"))

# Prepare long format
long_df <- plot_df %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = any_of(c("TWIST1", "OVOL1")), 
               names_to = "Gene", 
               values_to = "Expression")

# Define the pairwise comparisons you actually care about
my_comparisons <- list( c("NS", "AK"), c("AK", "cSCC"), c("NS", "cSCC") )

# Boxplot with Kruskal-Wallis + Pairwise Wilcoxon (FDR Adjusted)
ggplot(long_df, aes(x = Condition, y = Expression, fill = Condition)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.2, alpha = 0.3, size = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~Gene, scales = "free_y") +
  # 1. Global test (Kruskal-Wallis is better for non-normal gene data)
  stat_compare_means(method = "kruskal.test", label.y.npc = "top") + 
  # 2. Pairwise tests with FDR (BH) adjustment
  stat_compare_means(comparisons = my_comparisons, 
                     method = "wilcox.test", 
                     p.adjust.method = "BH", # False Discovery Rate correction
                     label = "p.signif") +
  theme_minimal() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("NS" = "#66c2a5", "AK" = "#fc8d62", "cSCC" = "#8da0cb")) +
  labs(title = "Gene Expression Progression in cSCC",
       subtitle = "Pairwise Wilcoxon tests with Benjamini-Hochberg (FDR) correction",
       y = "Batch-Corrected Log2 Expression")

# --- Faceted Correlation Plot ---
ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = TWIST1, y = OVOL1)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = Condition), size = 3, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "black", linetype = "dashed", se = TRUE) +
  # Spearman is non-parametric and often more significant for these "switches"
  stat_cor(method = "spearman", 
           label.x.npc = "left", 
           label.y.npc = "top",
           color = "blue",
           size = 4) +
  facet_wrap(~Condition, scales = "free") + 
  theme_bw() +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("NS" = "#66c2a5", "AK" = "#fc8d62", "cSCC" = "#8da0cb")) +
  labs(title = "TWIST1 vs OVOL1 Correlation Across Stages",
       subtitle = "Spearman Correlation (Outlier-Removed & Batch-Corrected)") +
  theme(strip.background = element_rect(fill = "gray90"), legend.position = "none")
```
CORRELATION HEAT MAP
```{r}
library(pheatmap)
library(RColorBrewer)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 6: INTEGRATED CORRELATION HEATMAP (CLEAN VERSION)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------

# 1. Calculate the Correlation Matrix using the final cleaned data
# Spearman is used to handle non-linear relationships and remains robust after ComBat
cor_mat <- cor(t(final_exprs), method = "spearman")

# 2. Define a high-contrast color palette (Navy for Negative, Firebrick for Positive)
heatmap_colors <- colorRampPalette(c("#053061", "#f7f7f7", "#67001f"))(100)

# 3. Generate the Heatmap
# Clustering is set to 'correlation' to group genes that behave similarly
pheatmap(cor_mat, 
         main = "Meta-Analysis: Gene Correlation Matrix",
         color = heatmap_colors,
         display_numbers = TRUE,        # Shows Rho values (-1 to 1)
         number_color = "black",
         fontsize_number = 10,
         clustering_distance_rows = "correlation", 
         clustering_distance_cols = "correlation",
         clustering_method = "complete",
         treeheight_row = 40,           # Visualizes the 'closeness' of genes
         treeheight_col = 40,
         border_color = "white")
```
CORRELATION HEAT MAP BY STAGE
```{r}
library(pheatmap)
library(dplyr)

# 1. Define the specific markers for this analysis
diff_markers <- c("KLF4", "IVL", "LOR", "KRT1", "KRT10")
all_targets <- c("TWIST1", "OVOL1", diff_markers)

# Ensure all markers are present in your common_genes
available_targets <- intersect(all_targets, rownames(final_exprs))

# 2. Create a function to generate the heatmap for a specific condition
plot_condition_cor <- function(condition_name, data, meta, genes) {
  
  # Subset samples for the specific condition
  samples <- rownames(meta[meta$Condition == condition_name, ])
  cond_data <- data[genes, samples]
  
  # Calculate Pearson Correlation
  cor_mat <- cor(t(cond_data), method = "pearson")
  
  # Generate Heatmap
  pheatmap(cor_mat, 
           main = paste("Pearson Correlation:", condition_name, "Stage"),
           color = colorRampPalette(c("#053061", "#f7f7f7", "#67001f"))(100),
           display_numbers = TRUE,
           number_color = "black",
           fontsize_number = 10,
           clustering_distance_rows = "correlation",
           clustering_distance_cols = "correlation",
           border_color = "white")
}

# 3. Generate the heatmaps for AK and cSCC
# (Note: These will appear as separate plots in your R environment)
plot_condition_cor("AK", final_exprs, final_meta, available_targets)
plot_condition_cor("cSCC", final_exprs, final_meta, available_targets)
```
